stem:
Kriti watches water vapour rise, cool high in the air, and form white clouds. Later she sees rain; her book also names hail and snow as forms that can fall.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: Cooling water vapour condenses into tiny liquid droplets that make up clouds.
From clouds, water can fall as rain, and in colder conditions as hail or snow.
Clouds are only thick patches of water vapour that never become liquid droplets.
A cloud rains only because it looks dark from the ground.

teacher.key_rationale: Water vapour cools and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds; precipitation can be rain, hail, or snow. Clouds are not uncondensed vapour alone, and darkness from the ground is not what causes rain.
